title: Fibonacci numbers: naive recursion vs dynamic programming vs fast doubling
problem_statement: Given a non-negative integer n, compute F(n) mod 2^64, where F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1, F(k) = F(k-1) + F(k-2).

input.parameter: n, the index (a value, not a length).
input.size_measure: Complexities below are stated in the VALUE n. In binary the input occupies b = ceil(log2(n+1)) bits; see caveats for the bit-size view.

algorithms.name: naive recursion
algorithms.idea: Evaluate the defining recurrence directly. Subproblems are recomputed, so the call tree has F(n+1) leaves.
algorithms.pseudocode: fib(n): if n < 2 return n; return fib(n-1) + fib(n-2)
algorithms.correctness: Direct transcription of the definition (reduced mod 2^64 at every step). The number of calls C(n) satisfies C(n) = C(n-1) + C(n-2) + 1, so C(n) = 2F(n+1) - 1 = Theta(phi^n), since phi^(n-2) <= F(n) <= phi^(n-1) for n >= 1 (PROOFS.md section 2).

algorithms.name: bottom-up dynamic programming
algorithms.idea: Compute F(0), F(1), ..., F(n) in order, keeping only the last two values. Each subproblem is solved once.
algorithms.pseudocode: a, b = 0, 1; repeat n times: a, b = b, a + b; return a
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n) word operations: exactly n loop iterations (range iteration at O(1) per step: machine-model assumption in background)
algorithms.correctness: Loop invariant: after k iterations (a, b) = (F(k), F(k+1)) mod 2^64 (PROOFS.md section 3).

algorithms.name: fast doubling (matrix power)
algorithms.idea: Use F(2k) = F(k)(2F(k+1) - F(k)) and F(2k+1) = F(k)^2 + F(k+1)^2 while scanning the bits of n; equivalent to computing [[1, 1],[1, 0]]^n by repeated squaring.
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(log n) word operations: exactly n.bit_length() loop iterations (n >= 1), with bin(n) built in O(log n) (machine-model assumption in background)
algorithms.space_complexity: O(1) words of arithmetic state, plus the string bin(n) of floor(log2 n) + 3 characters that the implementation builds (as large as the input up to a constant factor)
algorithms.correctness: The doubling identities follow from [[1, 1],[1, 0]]^k = [[F(k+1),F(k)],[F(k),F(k-1)]]. Invariant: after processing the top j bits of n (value k), (a, b) = (F(k), F(k+1)) mod 2^64 (PROOFS.md section 4).

relationship: Naive recursion is exponential, Theta(phi^n). Memoising the recurrence (DP) gives Theta(n); exploiting the matrix structure gives Theta(log n). The waste in the naive method is pure recomputation of overlapping subproblems: it calls itself only on 0..n, n + 1 distinct arguments, but 2F(n+1) - 1 times. Proofs of every claim: PROOFS.md.

sources.authors: Cormen, T. H.; Leiserson, C. E.; Rivest, R. L.; Stein, C.

The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 1: Fundamental Algorithms (3rd ed.)

sources.note: Background only (machine-model assumption). Read on 2026-10-07: bin converts an integer to a binary string prefixed with '0b' (a non-int argument must define __index__); a range object always takes the same small amount of memory.

verification.method: V1: all three implementations agree on n = 0..25 and selected large n, and match OEIS A000045 for n <= 25. V2: measured runtimes fitted against phi^n, n and log n respectively. Exact-count V2 by harness instrumentation was examined in round 2026-10-06c and is not possible with the implementation unchanged (observed on CPython 3.14.2; a measurement, not a proof): the only operation fast doubling performs on its input is bin(n), which makes one __index__ call on an instrumented non-int value and none on an int subclass; the loop runs over the characters of the str that bin() builds in C, and all arithmetic is on a and b, which start from the literals 0 and 1, and on the module constant MASK. The bottom-up DP likewise touches its input only through range(n) (one __index__ call). See experiments/2026-10-06c_value_reach_probe.py and research/2026-10-06c_count_v2_remaining.md. Proofs: PROOFS.md proves every claim of the entry (correctness, the exact call and iteration counts, time, space and the bit-size view, the time bounds under the machine-model assumption on bin and range in background) and records the observation above (CPython 3.14.2; measured, not proved) about what an instrumented input observes; tests/test_proofs_fib.py checks the computable facts on stated ranges.

caveats: Bit-size view: with input size b = log2(n) bits the three costs are Theta(phi^(2^b)), Theta(2^b) and Theta(b). So the DP is polynomial in the value n but EXPONENTIAL in the input length; only fast doubling is polynomial in input size. The mod 2^64 makes every arithmetic step O(1); computing the exact (unbounded) F(n) costs more because F(n) has ~0.694n bits (n log2(phi) + O(1); PROOFS.md section 5).
notes: Canonical teaching example of T2: the naive method is wasteful, not the problem hard. Secondary tag T3 (added 2026-10-06, RL-056): DP Theta(n) -> fast doubling Theta(log n).

background.statement: Machine-model assumption of this entry: bin(n) returns the '0b'-prefixed binary string of n (floor(log2 n) + 1 digits for n >= 1) in O(log n) time and space, and range(n) is a constant-size object whose iteration yields 0, ..., n - 1 at O(1) per step. The documentation states the format of bin and that a range object always takes the same small amount of memory; the time bounds are assumed, not proved in this repository.
